subject: Animation
title: King Kong: Stop-Motion's Greatest Moment
description: A 60-second lesson on King Kong: Stop-Motion's Greatest Moment.

hook.text: In 1933, Willis O'Brien animated an eighteen-inch gorilla puppet and made the world believe it was giant.

buildup.text: O'Brien combined stop-motion puppets with live actors using glass paintings and rear projection.

discovery.text: Kong had emotion. O'Brien gave the puppet curiosity, rage, and tenderness that moved audiences deeply.

twist.text: The film was a massive hit during the Depression, proving spectacle could lift spirits and fill theaters.

climax.text: King Kong inspired every creature effects artist who followed, from Harryhausen to Spielberg.

punchline.text: An eighteen-inch puppet became cinema's biggest icon.

quiz.question: How tall was the King Kong puppet that Willis O'Brien animated?
options: Eighteen inches, made to appear giant through camera techniques
